name: California

dates.sub: Missed it? You can still register and vote the same day at a vote center or your county elections office, through Nov 3.

dates.what: Your ballot comes in the mail
dates.sub: Every registered voter gets one. Didn't get yours? Ask your county elections office for a new one.
Places and hours vary by county. Many counties open more vote centers on Oct 24.
Mail it postmarked by Nov 3 (it must arrive by Nov 10), or drop it off by 8 p.m. that day.

groups.title: Federal
groups.sub: They make laws for the entire country.

groups.title: State
groups.sub: They run California. Everyone in the state votes on these.

groups.title: State lawmakers
groups.sub: They write California's laws. Your district decides who's on your ballot.

groups.title: Propositions
groups.sub: Yes-or-no questions that change California's laws or constitution.

footerNote: If your address can't be matched, we fall back to ZIP code. ZIP codes can cross district lines, so double-check yours on your voter page.

notes.title: Why two people from the same party can face off.
notes.text: In California's primary, everyone runs on one list and the top two go on to November, whatever their party. So some races have two Democrats or two Republicans.

notes.title: New U.S. House districts this year.
notes.text: California redrew its U.S. House districts for 2026, so your district number may have changed. The address lookup uses the new lines.
